title: Orderly Queue
statement: You get a string `s` of lowercase letters and an integer `k`. A move removes any one character from among the first `k` characters of `s` and appends it to the end of `s`. You may make any number of moves, including none. Return the lexicographically smallest string that can be reached.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

With `k = 1` the only move sends the front character to the back, so the string just rotates: the reachable strings are exactly the rotations of `s`, and we pick the smallest. With `k >= 2` we can hold one character back while cycling the others past it, which lets us swap any two neighbours. Adjacent swaps can produce every arrangement, so the answer is simply the sorted string. Searching all reachable strings would work on tiny inputs, but it explodes quickly.

## Approach

1. If `k > 1`, sort the characters of `s` and return them joined.
2. Otherwise start `best` as `s` itself (the rotation by 0).
3. For each shift `i` from 1 to `s.length - 1`, build `rotated` by moving the first `i` characters to the end.
4. Keep `rotated` in `best` when it compares smaller.
5. Return `best`.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "cba"`, `k = 1`, so only rotations count. `best` starts as `"cba"`. With `i = 1` the rotation is `"bac"`, smaller, so `best = "bac"`. With `i = 2` it is `"acb"`, smaller again, so `best = "acb"`, which is returned.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) when `k > 1` (sorting); O(n²) when `k = 1` (n rotations, each built and compared in O(n)).
- Space: O(n) for the sorted copy or the current rotation.

## Pitfalls

- `k = 1` is genuinely different: sorting there gives strings that cannot be reached.
- `k = 2` already allows every permutation; there is no need to treat larger `k` separately.
- Rotations must wrap around: `s.slice(i) + s.slice(0, i)`, not just a suffix.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `k` | how many front characters a move may choose from |
| `best` | smallest rotation seen so far |
| `i` | how many front characters are moved to the back |
| `rotated` | the rotation of `s` by `i` |

narration.2: With two or more choices any two neighbours can be swapped, so every arrangement is reachable.
narration.3: The smallest arrangement is the characters in sorted order.
narration.5: With k = 1 only rotations are reachable; the unrotated string is the first candidate.
narration.6: Try every other rotation amount i.
narration.7: Move the first i characters to the back to form this rotation.
narration.8: Is this rotation smaller than the best so far?
narration.9: Yes: keep it as the new best.
narration.12: Every rotation was compared; return the smallest.
